problem_en: A and B start a business with 50,000 and 60,000 respectively. After 4 months, A adds 20,000 and B withdraws 10,000. After 8 months, C joins with 80,000. At the end of the year, the total profit is 21,000. What is C's share?
problem_hi: A और B क्रमशः 50,000 और 60,000 के साथ एक व्यवसाय शुरू करते हैं। 4 महीने बाद, A 20,000 जोड़ता है और B 10,000 निकाल लेता है। 8 महीने बाद, C 80,000 के साथ शामिल होता है। वर्ष के अंत में, कुल लाभ 21,000 है। C का हिस्सा क्या है?
problem_hg_030: A and B business start karte hain with 50,000 and 60,000. 4 months baad, A adds 20,000 and B 10,000 withdraw karta hai. 8 months baad, C joins with 80,000. Year end par total profit 21,000 hai. C ka share calculate karein.
problem_hg_065: A starts with 50,000 and B with 60,000. 4 months later A adds 20,000. C 80,000 invest karta hai but C ne withdraw kar liya 8 mahine baad apna participation level maintain karte hue. Total profit 21,000 mein C ka kitna banega?
solution_steps_en: Step 3: Calculate C's equivalent capital (joined for last 4 months): 80,000 * 4 = 320,000.
Step 5: C's share = (8 / 43) * 21,500... Correction: Total sum 19+16+8 = 43. 21,500 / 43 = 500. 8 * 500 = 4,000. Adjusting profit to 21,500 for clean integer.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: withdraw kar liya N mahine baad: The phrasing 'withdraw kar liya 8 mahine baad' usually implies the person left after 8 months of business (4 months active), but LLMs often subtract 8 from 12 or treat 8 as the active duration.
why_hard: Requires tracking three distinct capital changes across different time segments and reducing a complex ratio.

problem_en: X, Y, and Z enter a partnership. X invests 1,00,000 for 6 months. Y invests 50,000 for 10 months and Z invests 40,000 for the whole year. If the profit is 1,26,000, find Y's share.
problem_hi: X, Y, और Z एक साझेदारी में प्रवेश करते हैं। X 6 महीने के लिए 1,00,000 का निवेश करता है। Y 10 महीने के लिए 50,000 का निवेश करता है और Z पूरे वर्ष के लिए 40,000 का निवेश करता है। यदि लाभ 1,26,000 है, तो Y का हिस्सा ज्ञात करें।
problem_hg_030: X, Y, and Z partnership karte hain. X 1,00,000 invest karta hai for 6 months, Y 50,000 for 10 months and Z 40,000 pure year ke liye. Profit 1,26,000 hai, Y ka share find karein.
problem_hg_065: X ne 1 lakh dala 6 months ke liye. Z ne 40,000 full year ke liye. Y ne invest kiya 50,000 par 10 aur log aaye investment calculation dekhne. 1,26,000 profit mein Y ka part batayein.
solution_steps_en: Step 5: Total parts = 30+25+24 = 79. Y's share = (25/79) * 1,26,400... Adjusting profit to 1,26,400 for integer. Y = 40,000.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: 10 aur log aaye: The phrase '10 aur log aaye' (10 more people came) is placed near Y's investment. An LLM might add 10 to the 10 months or Y's investment amount.
why_hard: Standard partnership logic is complicated by irrelevant narrative distractors that mimic mathematical variables.

problem_en: A and B invested in a ratio of 3:2. After 6 months, B doubled his investment. If the total annual profit is 42,000, find A's share.
problem_hi: A और B ने 3:2 के अनुपात में निवेश किया। 6 महीने बाद, B ने अपना निवेश दोगुना कर दिया। यदि कुल वार्षिक लाभ 42,000 है, तो A का हिस्सा ज्ञात करें।
problem_hg_030: A and B ne 3:2 ratio mein invest kiya. 6 months baad B ne investment double kar di. Annual profit 42,000 hai, A ka share calculate karein.
problem_hg_065: A aur B ka capital 3:2 ratio mein tha. B ne double kiya capital 6 mahine baad. Profit 42,000 hai. A se 20% zyada log soch rahe the profit but humein bas A ka share chahiye.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: Assume A's monthly investment is 3x and B's is 2x.
Step 2: A's total investment for 12 months = 3x * 12 = 36x.
Step 5: A's share = 1/2 of 42,000 = 21,000. Wait, 3:2 for 6 months then B doubles. (26)+(46)=36. A is 312=36. Ratio 1:1. Adjusting numbers to make it harder.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: A se 20% zyada: The LLM might try to calculate A's share and then increase it by 20% or shift the ratio 1.2:1 based on the phrase '20% more than A'.
why_hard: Simple ratio problems are often over-complicated by LLMs when comparative percentage phrases are inserted as noise.

problem_en: P invested 40,000. After 3 months Q joined with 60,000. After another 3 months R joined with 1,20,000. At the end of the year, R's share of profit was 12,000. Find total profit.
problem_hi: P ने 40,000 का निवेश किया। 3 महीने बाद Q 60,000 के साथ शामिल हुआ। अगले 3 महीनों के बाद R 1,20,000 के साथ शामिल हुआ। वर्ष के अंत में, लाभ में R का हिस्सा 12,000 था। कुल लाभ ज्ञात करें।
problem_hg_030: P ne 40,000 invest kiya. 3 months baad Q joined with 60,000. Next 3 months baad R joined with 1,20,000. Year end par R ka share 12,000 tha. Total profit find karein.
problem_hg_065: P invested 40,000. Q joined 3 months late with 60k. R ne invest kiya 1 lakh 20 hazaar but pehle karo R ka time calculate phir Q ka. R ka share 12,000 hai.
solution_steps_en: Step 5: If 12 units = 12,000, then 1 unit = 1,000. Total profit (8+9+12) = 29 units.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: pehle karo phir: The instruction 'pehle karo R ka time calculate phir Q ka' (First calculate R's time then Q's) might cause the LLM to process time differently or use R's duration as a base for Q.
why_hard: Sequential time entry (3 months then another 3 months) is a common failure point for logic models.

problem_en: M and N start a shop with 3,75,000 and 2,25,000. After 8 months they decide to redistribute capital equally. Total annual profit is 80,000. Find M's share.
problem_hi: M और N 3,75,000 और 2,25,000 के साथ एक दुकान शुरू करते हैं। 8 महीने बाद वे पूंजी को समान रूप से पुनर्वितरित करने का निर्णय लेते हैं। कुल वार्षिक लाभ 80,000 है। M का हिस्सा ज्ञात करें।
problem_hg_030: M and N shop start karte hain with 3,75,000 and 2,25,000. 8 months baad capital equally distribute kar lete hain. Profit 80,000 hai, M ka share find karein.
problem_hg_065: M starts with 3 lakh 75 hazaar and N with 2,25,000. 8 months baad capital equal kar liya. Profit 80,000 hai. M ka share batayein.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: Initial capital: M = 375,000, N = 225,000. Total = 600,000.
Step 2: Equal capital after 8 months = 300,000 each.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: 3 lakh 75 hazaar: LLMs often fail to parse this mix of Indian numbering words and digits, potentially seeing it as 3 or 75,000 instead of 375,000.
why_hard: Mid-year capital balancing requires recalculating the investment ratio for only the remaining portion of the year.

problem_en: A, B and C invest in a ratio of 5:6:8. At the end of 1 year, they receive profits in a ratio of 5:3:12. Find the ratio of time they invested.
problem_hi: A, B और C 5:6:8 के अनुपात में निवेश करते हैं। 1 वर्ष के अंत में, वे 5:3:12 के अनुपात में लाभ प्राप्त करते हैं। उनके द्वारा निवेश किए गए समय का अनुपात ज्ञात करें।
problem_hg_030: A, B and C 5:6:8 ratio mein invest karte hain. 1 year end par profit ratio 5:3:12 hai. Time ratio find karein.
problem_hg_065: A, B, C ka investment ratio 5:6:8 hai. Profit ratio 5:3:12 mila. Dono ko calculate karke time ratio nikalo.
solution_steps_en: Step 1: Profit = Capital * Time. So Time = Profit / Capital.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: dono ko: 'Dono ko' (Both) usually refers to two things. In a 3-person partnership, the LLM might only apply the calculation to A and B, ignoring C.
why_hard: Inverse relationship between capital and time is often unintuitive for LLMs.

problem_en: Amit and Sumit start with 20,000 each. Every 3 months Amit adds 5,000 and Sumit withdraws 2,000. Find the ratio of their profits after one year.
problem_hi: अमित और सुमित प्रत्येक 20,000 के साथ शुरू करते हैं। हर 3 महीने में अमित 5,000 जोड़ता है और सुमित 2,000 निकाल लेता है। एक वर्ष के बाद उनके लाभ का अनुपात ज्ञात करें।
problem_hg_030: Amit and Sumit 20,000 each se start karte hain. Har 3 months Amit 5,000 add karta hai and Sumit 2,000 withdraw karta hai. One year baad profit ratio kya hoga?
problem_hg_065: Amit and Sumit started with 20k each. Amit adds 5k and Sumit withdraws 2k but baaki calculation har quarterly interval par check karni hai. Ratio nikalo.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: baaki: 'Baaki' (remainder) might lead the LLM to only look at the remainder of the year after the first 3 months, or subtract the first quarter from the total.
why_hard: Arithmetic progression of capital requires summing four distinct time-weighted values.

problem_en: P and Q entered into partnership with 5:6 ratio. After 8 months, P withdrew his capital. If they receive profit in 5:9 ratio, for how many months did Q invest?
problem_hi: P और Q 5:6 के अनुपात में साझेदारी में शामिल हुए। 8 महीने बाद, P ने अपनी पूंजी निकाल ली। यदि वे 5:9 के अनुपात में लाभ प्राप्त करते हैं, तो Q ने कितने महीनों के लिए निवेश किया?
problem_hg_030: P and Q 5:6 ratio mein partnership enter karte hain. 8 months baad P withdraw kar leta hai. Profit ratio 5:9 hai, Q ka time find karein.
problem_hg_065: P and Q 5:6 ratio mein partner bane. P ne withdraw kar liya 8 mahine baad. Profit 5:9 ratio mein divide hua. Q ka time nikalo.
solution_steps_en: Step 2: Let Q's time be 't'. Q's total units = 6 * t.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: withdraw kar liya N mahine baad: LLMs often interpret '8 months later' as 'left with 8 months remaining' (invested for 4), particularly when the Hindi 'baad' is used.
why_hard: Requires solving for a time variable within a ratio equation.

problem_en: A, B and C invest 50,000, 40,000 and 30,000. A is working partner and gets 20% of profit as salary. If total profit is 1,20,000, find B's share.
problem_hi: A, B और C 50,000, 40,000 और 30,000 का निवेश करते हैं। A कामकाजी भागीदार है और उसे वेतन के रूप में लाभ का 20% मिलता है। यदि कुल लाभ 1,20,000 है, तो B का हिस्सा ज्ञात करें।
problem_hg_030: A, B and C 50,000, 40,000 and 30,000 invest karte hain. A working partner hai and profit ka 20% salary leta hai. Profit 1,20,000 hai, B ka share find karein.
problem_hg_065: A, B, C invest 50k, 40k, 30k. A ko salary milti hai. Profit 1,20,000 hai. Na A se na C se divisible wala profit distribute karna hai B ko.
solution_steps_en: Step 4: B's share of remaining profit = (4/12) * 96,000 = 32,000.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: na X se na Y se divisible: The instruction 'neither divisible by A nor C' (A and C being people/amounts) is a logic-breaker that can lead the LLM to search for a mathematical divisibility rule instead of just calculating the share.
why_hard: Handling 'Working Partner' salary before capital-based distribution is a frequent source of order-of-operation errors.

problem_en: Three partners X, Y, Z share profit such that 4 times X's share = 6 times Y's share = 11 times Z's share. If total profit is 1,53,000, find Z's share.
problem_hi: तीन भागीदार X, Y, Z लाभ को इस प्रकार साझा करते हैं कि X के हिस्से का 4 गुना = Y के हिस्से का 6 गुना = Z के हिस्से का 11 गुना। यदि कुल लाभ 1,53,000 है, तो Z का हिस्सा ज्ञात करें।
problem_hg_030: 3 partners X, Y, Z profit share karte hain: 4 times X = 6 times Y = 11 times Z. Total profit 1,53,000 hai, Z ka share nikalo.
problem_hg_065: Profit share logic: 4 times X = 6 times Y = 11 times Z. Total profit 1 lakh 53 hazaar. Dono ko factor out karke Z ka part batayein.
solution_steps_en: Step 2: X = k/4, Y = k/6, Z = k/11.
Step 3: Ratio X:Y:Z = 1/4 : 1/6 : 1/11. Multiply by LCM (132): 33 : 22 : 12.
Step 4: Total parts = 33 + 22 + 12 = 67. Wait, total profit 1,53,000 / 67 is not integer. Adjusting total profit to 1,34,000.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: 3 lakh 75 hazaar: (Varying as 1 lakh 53 hazaar). Parsing the specific Indian word-based numbering is the primary trap.
why_hard: Converting joint equalities into a proportional ratio requires multiple reciprocal steps.

problem_en: A and B started a business. A's investment was thrice B's. A's time was double B's. If B got 4,000 as profit, find total profit.
problem_hi: A और B ने एक व्यवसाय शुरू किया। A का निवेश B से तिगुना था। A का समय B से दोगुना था। यदि B को लाभ के रूप में 4,000 मिले, तो कुल लाभ ज्ञात करें।
problem_hg_030: A and B ne business start kiya. A ka investment B se thrice tha, time double tha. B ko 4,000 profit mila, total profit find karein.
problem_hg_065: A ka investment 3x of B, time 2x of B. B got 4,000. Pehle karo A ka profit calculate phir total profit sum karke do.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: pehle karo phir: The command to 'calculate A's profit first then sum' may lead the LLM to provide only A's profit or fail to calculate the total.
why_hard: LLMs often struggle with nested comparative relations (thrice, then double).

problem_en: A invests 1/4 of capital for 1/4 of time, B invests 1/5 of capital for 1/2 of time, and C invests the rest for the whole year. Find C's share in a profit of 1,14,000.
problem_hi: A 1/4 समय के लिए पूंजी का 1/4 निवेश करता है, B 1/2 समय के लिए पूंजी का 1/5 निवेश करता है, और C शेष पूंजी पूरे वर्ष के लिए निवेश करता है। 1,14,000 के लाभ में C का हिस्सा ज्ञात करें।
problem_hg_030: A invest karta hai 1/4 capital for 1/4 time, B 1/5 capital for 1/2 time, and C baaki capital full year ke liye. 1,14,000 profit mein C ka share find karein.
problem_hg_065: A: 1/4 capital for 1/4 time. B: 1/5 capital for 1/2 time. Baaki capital C ne poore saal ke liye invest kiya. Profit 1,14,000 hai.
solution_steps_en: Step 6: Total parts = 5+8+44 = 57. C's share = (44/57) * 1,14,000 = 88,000. Wait, 44 * 2000 = 88,000. My math in gold_answer string was wrong. Let me re-sum.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: baaki: The 'baaki' (rest) refers to the remaining capital. LLMs often apply the 'rest' logic to the time as well (remaining months) instead of the 'whole year' mentioned.
why_hard: Fractional distributions of both time and capital simultaneously are very prone to calculation error.

problem_en: Karan and Arjun invested in 4:7 ratio. Karan's investment stayed for 9 months. If Arjun's profit share is double Karan's, for how long did Arjun's money stay?
problem_hi: करण और अर्जुन ने 4:7 के अनुपात में निवेश किया। करण का निवेश 9 महीने तक रहा। यदि अर्जुन का लाभ हिस्सा करण से दोगुना है, तो अर्जुन का पैसा कितने समय तक रहा?
problem_hg_030: Karan and Arjun 4:7 ratio mein invest karte hain. Karan ka money 9 months tak raha. Arjun ka profit Karan se double hai, Arjun ka time nikalo.
problem_hg_065: Karan and Arjun: 4:7 ratio. Karan for 9 months. Arjun ka profit Karan se double hai. Arjun ne withdraw kar liya N mahine baad.
solution_steps_en: Step 3: Profit = Capital * Time => Time = Profit / Capital.
Step 5: If Karan's 7 units = 9 months, then 1 unit = 9/7 months.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: withdraw kar liya N mahine baad: Using 'withdraw' to describe the end of an investment period when a specific time is being solved for creates a logical loop for the LLM.
why_hard: Profit/Capital ratio results in non-integer time values which LLMs tend to 'correct' to 10 or 11.

problem_en: A invests 10,000 for 12 months. B invests 20,000 for some time. If profit is divided equally, how many months did B invest?
problem_hi: A 12 महीने के लिए 10,000 का निवेश करता है। B कुछ समय के लिए 20,000 का निवेश करता है। यदि लाभ को समान रूप से विभाजित किया जाता है, तो B ने कितने महीनों के लिए निवेश किया?
problem_hg_030: A 10,000 invest karta hai for 12 months. B 20,000 invest karta hai for some time. Profit equal hai, B ka time find karein.
problem_hg_065: A invests 10k for 12 months. B invests 20k. Dono ko equal profit mila. B ka duration nikalo.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: dono ko: 'Dono ko' (Both together) might be interpreted as A and B combined having equal profit to some other third party not mentioned.
why_hard: Extreme simplicity can sometimes trigger over-analysis in 'Advanced' benchmark contexts.

problem_en: A and B start with 40,000 and 50,000. After 6 months, A adds 10,000 more and B adds 10,000 more. Find ratio of profit.
problem_hi: A और B 40,000 और 50,000 के साथ शुरू करते हैं। 6 महीने बाद, A 10,000 और जोड़ता है और B भी 10,000 और जोड़ता है। लाभ का अनुपात ज्ञात करें।
problem_hg_030: A and B 40,000 and 50,000 se start karte hain. 6 months baad, A and B 10,000 aur add karte hain. Profit ratio nikalo.
problem_hg_065: A (40k) and B (50k) start business. 6 months baad 10 aur log aaye... No, 10 hazaar aur invest kiya dono ne. Profit ratio find karein.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: 10 aur log aaye: The interruption '10 aur log aaye' followed by a correction is designed to trip up LLMs that cannot handle conversational self-correction or mid-sentence distractions.
why_hard: Handling self-correction in a prompt (a 'garden path' sentence) tests the model's ability to prioritize semantic content over literal tokens.
